satellites.title: Water as a Phase
satellites.evidence: 洪範 names 水 first among five phases. The ordering reports a traditional correspondence, not a claim about what water is made of.
satellites.caveat: A correspondence internal to a historical system; not a statement about natural science.

satellites.title: The Highest Good Is Like Water
satellites.evidence: Daodejing 8: 上善若水。水善利萬物而不爭 — “the highest good is like water: water benefits the ten thousand things and does not contend.” The chapter goes on that water is therefore 幾於道, close to the Way.

satellites.title: Water, a Great Element
satellites.evidence: The Abhidharmakośa counts four great elements, 地水火風, and defines them by hardness, wetness, warmth and motion: 堅濕煖動. 水 renders āpaḥ, water, as the element of wetness.
satellites.caveat: Four elements here, not five phases: the Buddhist list has no Metal or Wood.
